annotationRationale: Regular-hexagon geometry and midsegments determine triangle XYZ. Special right triangles determine the three corner areas, which are subtracted to obtain the intersection.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution. Adds a midpoint construction to justify the trapezoid midline and explains the angles, congruence, and corner removal without relying on the official diagram.

review.mathCheck: The midsegments give XZ=3/2, and rotational symmetry makes XYZ equilateral. Each removed corner has perpendicular legs 1/4 and √3/4, hence area √3/32. The corner portions occupy only 3/4 of each side of length 3/2, so the cuts are disjoint. Subtraction gives 15√3/32, choice C; excluding boundaries does not affect area.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of the first MAA approach on page 12. Candidate U,V correspond to the figure's U1,U2. Two triangle midsegments replace the trapezoid midline, and the official congruent-corner argument is explained explicitly.
review.annotationCheck: Composite-area subtraction and 30° right-triangle properties are correctly assessed. Midsegments and regular-polygon geometry support them. The displayed Pythagorean calculation is appropriate background.
